sections.overview: The accepted species is native to the Saramacca and Suriname rivers and the Marowijne basin of Suriname and French Guiana.
sections.identification: The scientific name refers to Suriname, its type locality; “Perle du Suriname” is a French aquarium common name.
sections.habitat: Adults are reported from muddy or sandy bottomed canals and quiet cascade zones.
sections.diet: It is omnivorous with a tendency toward plant food and searches the substrate by digging with its protrusible mouth.
sections.behavior: FishBase reports that it sometimes occurs with G. harreri in quieter parts of cascades.
sections.reproduction: It is a larvophilic mouthbrooder: parents take eggs into the mouth after spawning and later shelter larvae there.
sections.ecology: It shares quieter cascade reaches with G. harreri, which is also recorded in this basin.
sections.conservation: FishBase lists global Least Concern, assessed on 12 March 2023.
